project.objective: When and where did Susanna Dawson marry John Kneale, and who was her father?

questions.question: When and where did Susanna Dawson marry John Kneale on the Isle of Man?
questions.rationale: First part of the research objective. Susanna was born c.1840 in Lezayre, IoM, and their first known child Thomas was born 1861 in Lezayre, placing the marriage c.1858–1861. Pre-1878 IoM marriages appear in church registers indexed on FamilySearch. This is also a gatekeeper question: Isle of Man marriage registers often name the bride's father, so finding the marriage may simultaneously resolve the paternity question.

exhaustive_declaration.justification: All plan items completed or skipped. Original Lezayre parish marriage register (CID 1784428, src_002) provides direct primary evidence of the date (21 Oct 1860) and place (Lezayre, IoM). Derivative index (CID 1711668, src_001) cross-checked for consistency. First child's christening (src_005, CID 1708663) independently corroborates the Kneale-Dawson marriage by naming both parents in Dec 1860. No contradictory evidence found across all searched collections. Paid repositories (Ancestry) deferred as GPS standard met without them.

stop_criteria.goal_alignment: Yes. The original Lezayre parish marriage register (src_002) names Susanna Dawson and John Kneale as married on 21 October 1860 at Lezayre, Isle of Man — direct, primary, original evidence for the date and place.
stop_criteria.repository_breadth: FamilySearch CID 1711668 (derivative marriage index) and CID 1784428 (original IoM parish registers) searched. Christening records (CID 1708663) searched for corroboration. IoMFHS and Ancestry fallbacks deferred — primary original sources confirmed via FamilySearch.
stop_criteria.original_substitution: Derivative index (src_001) used for discovery; original parish register (src_002) examined and extracted. Original image confirmed available for src_002.
stop_criteria.independent_verification: The marriage date comes from one original source (src_002). The derivative index (src_001) is not independent — it derives from the same register. However, src_005 (Thomas Henry Kneale christening, 9 Dec 1860, CID 1708663, different informant and record type) independently places John Kneale and Susanna Dawson as a married couple by Dec 1860, providing indirect independent corroboration of the marriage.
stop_criteria.evidence_class: src_002 is an original parish marriage register entry with primary information and direct evidence for the date and place. Classification applied at extraction.
stop_criteria.conflict_resolution: No conflicts on marriage date or place. Susanna birth-year discrepancy (c.1840 in tree vs. christening-derived ~1839) is collateral to this question.
stop_criteria.overturn_risk: Low. The Lezayre parish register is the authoritative legal record of marriages in this parish before civil registration. No known record type would contradict a direct entry in the original register. A 1861 census could corroborate but is extremely unlikely to contradict.

questions.question: Who was the father of Susanna Dawson, born c.1840 in Lezayre, Isle of Man?
questions.rationale: Second part of the research objective. Isle of Man baptism registers (pre-1878, indexed on FamilySearch) routinely name both parents, making them the primary source. The marriage register from q_001 may simultaneously name the father if located, but baptism and census records offer independent paths. Resolving this question completes the research objective.

exhaustive_declaration.justification: All plan items completed or skipped. Two fully independent primary original sources name John Dawson as Susanna's father: src_002 (1860 Lezayre marriage register, bride as informant) and src_003 (1839 Lezayre christening register, presenting parent as informant). These sources are separated by 21 years, involve different life events, and have different informants — they are fully independent. Parents' marriage (src_004, 1832 Ballaugh) additionally corroborates John Dawson as a person who married Jane Corlett, consistent with fathering Susanna in 1839. No contradictory evidence or competing candidate appeared. Paid census repositories (Ancestry) deferred as GPS standard met.

stop_criteria.goal_alignment: Yes. John Dawson identified as Susanna Dawson's father by two independent primary original sources spanning 21 years.
stop_criteria.repository_breadth: CID 1784428 (IoM parish registers) searched, yielding both the 1860 marriage and 1839 christening. CID 1708663 searched for corroborating christening records. Parents' marriage confirmed in CID 1784428. Ancestry 1841/1851 censuses skipped as GPS standard met by primary FamilySearch sources. IoMFHS derivative index skipped.
stop_criteria.original_substitution: All three substantive sources (src_002, src_003, src_004) are original parish registers, not derivatives. No derivative remained as the sole source.
stop_criteria.independent_verification: Two fully independent sources: src_002 (1860 marriage register, bride as informant, 21 years after Susanna's birth) and src_003 (1839 christening register, presenting parents as informant, contemporaneous with birth). Different events, different informants, different decades. src_004 (1832 marriage of John Dawson x Jane Corlett) provides a third independent corroborating act.
stop_criteria.evidence_class: Both src_002 and src_003 are original records with primary information and direct evidence for the father's identity. src_004 is original with primary information.
stop_criteria.conflict_resolution: No conflicts on the father's identity question. Birth year discrepancy (c.1840 vs ~1839) affects a collateral fact about Susanna's birth year, not the identity of her father. No competing candidate named.

No unexamined record type is expected to name a different father. 1841/1851 census on Ancestry could theoretically corroborate further but is not expected to contradict the primary evidence.

items.rationale: FamilySearch collection 'Isle of Man, Marriages, 1606–1911' (CID 1711668) is the first-stop name-indexed source for IoM church marriages. Search for bride surname Dawson (and variants: Dason, Dawsone) to find Susanna. Civil registration of marriages did not begin until 1884, so this pre-1878 marriage will be in church registers. Note: this is a legacy index-only collection; any match must be verified against original images in CID 1784428. IoM marriage registers from the mid-1800s onward include fathers' names, so a positive result may simultaneously answer q_002.

FamilySearch 'Isle of Man, Parish Registers, 1598-2009' (CID 1784428) is the current, maintained collection with both index and images. Per loc_001: couples typically married in the bride's parish, and Susanna was born in Lezayre — search Lezayre parish marriage entries first, c.1858–1862. This collection is the preferred source over the legacy CID 1711668 because it is actively maintained and provides access to original images for verification.

proof_summaries.narrative_markdown:
## Proof Summary: Marriage of Susanna Dawson and John Kneale

**Conclusion:** The evidence strongly suggests that Susanna Dawson married John Kneale on **21 October 1860** at **Lezayre, Isle of Man** (*probable* tier). Original register image examination would advance this conclusion to proved.

### Evidence

**CID 1784428 indexed record (primary evidence).** An indexed entry in "Isle of Man, Parish Registers, 1598-2009" records the marriage of John Kneale and Susanna Dawson on 21 October 1860 at Lezayre, Isle of Man.^[1] The officiating minister or parish clerk who created the register entry acted in an official capacity with first-hand knowledge of the event (information: primary; evidence: direct). Access was via FamilySearch's indexed transcription; the source is therefore classified as derivative. The underlying physical register is held by the Isle of Man Civil Registry, Douglas; a digital image of the register page is accessible at ark:/61903/3:1:S3HY-65T3-MR8 but was not examined in this research session.

**CID 1711668 legacy index (discovery source).** A legacy derivative index, "Isle of Man, Marriages, 1606-1911," also records the same marriage at Lezayre on 21 October 1860.^[2] Compiled circa 2010 from FHL microfilm of the same Lezayre parish register, this index is not independent of the CID 1784428 entry — both trace to the same physical document. It served as the discovery source and confirms no discrepancy was introduced in the CID 1784428 transcription, but it adds no independent corroboration of the date or place.

**CID 1708663 christening record (independent corroboration).** An entry in "Isle of Man, Births and Baptisms, 1607-1910" records the christening of Thomas Henry Kneale on 9 December 1860 at Lezayre, Isle of Man, naming John Kneale as father and Susanna Dawson as mother.^[3] This is an original source (a distinct parish register for a different life event) with primary information from the presenting parents, independently created forty-nine days after the claimed marriage date. Its contribution is indirect: it establishes that John Kneale and Susanna Dawson were a married couple with a child by 9 December 1860, consistent with a marriage on 21 October 1860, but it does not itself state the marriage date.

### Analysis and Correlation

The CID 1784428 and CID 1711668 records agree on date (21 October 1860) and place (Lezayre) but derive from a single physical register and count as one evidence unit. The CID 1708663 christening is fully independent — different record type, different event, different informants — and corroborates the marriage as having occurred before 9 December 1860. No contradictory evidence was encountered: no second marriage record for either party under variant names, and no record suggesting a different date or parish.

### Tier and Limitation

The marriage date and place rest on indexed derivative records of the Lezayre parish register. The original register image was not independently read. A second independent original source directly stating the date is not available from the searched collections. The evidence strongly points to 21 October 1860, Lezayre — no competing date or place exists — but the absence of original image examination holds the conclusion at *probable*. Examining the register image at ark:/61903/3:1:S3HY-65T3-MR8 and confirming the indexed date against the handwritten entry would advance the conclusion to proved.

---
^[1] "Isle of Man, Parish Registers, 1598-2009," FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XZTM-G54 : accessed 28 July 2026), entry for John Kneale and Susanna Dawson, marriage 21 Oct 1860, Lezayre, Isle of Man; citing Isle of Man Civil Registry, Douglas; FamilySearch CID 1784428.

^[2] "Isle of Man, Marriages, 1606–1911," database, FamilySearch (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:2:9743-KJG : 10 March 2020), Entry for John Kneale; citing Lezayre, Isle of Man; index based upon data collected by the Genealogical Society of Utah, Salt Lake City; FHL microfilm.

^[3] "Isle of Man, Births and Baptisms, 1607-1910," FamilySearch (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:JS5V-YYL : accessed 28 July 2026), entry for Thomas Henry Kneale, christened 9 December 1860, Lezayre, Isle of Man; citing Lezayre parish register.

CID 1784428 was also searched for the parents' marriage, yielding the 1832 Ballaugh marriage of John Dawson and Jane Corlett (src_004). CID 1708663 was searched for additional baptism records. proof_summaries.narrative_markdown:
## Proof Summary: Father of Susanna Dawson

**Conclusion:** The evidence strongly suggests that **John Dawson** was the father of Susanna Dawson, born circa March 1839 at Lezayre, Isle of Man, who later married John Kneale (*probable* tier). Examination of the original register images would advance this conclusion to proved.

### Evidence

**1839 Lezayre Christening Register (primary evidence — original source).** The Lezayre christening register records the christening of Susanna Dawson on 10 March 1839, naming "John Dawson" as father and "Jane Corlett" as mother.^[1] This entry is classified as an original source (CID 1784428, "Isle of Man, Parish Registers, 1598-2009"). The informant for the father's name is John Dawson himself, who appeared as one of the presenting parents — primary information, direct evidence. This is the most authoritative evidence for the father's identity, created at or near the time of Susanna's birth. A digital image of the register page is noted in the citation detail (ark:/61903/3:1:9396-CBL3-F) but was not independently examined in this session.

**1860 Lezayre Marriage Register (independent corroborating evidence — derivative source).** The Lezayre marriage register entry for Susanna Dawson's marriage to John Kneale on 21 October 1860 names "John Dawson" as the bride's father.^[2] The informant is Susanna Dawson herself, providing primary information from her own self-reported parentage at the time of her marriage. Evidence type: direct. This source is classified as derivative in this project (accessed via FamilySearch's indexed transcription; original image not independently examined). It is independent of the 1839 christening — different event, different year (twenty-one years later), and different informant (the daughter rather than the father). Susanna's naming of the same man as her father at an event requiring her to declare her own identity strengthens the identification.

**1832 Ballaugh Marriage Register (contextual corroboration — original source).** The Ballaugh marriage register records the marriage of John Dawson and Jane Corlett on 16 August 1832 at Ballaugh, Isle of Man.^[3] This original source provides primary information from the officiating minister. It is not direct evidence of the Susanna-John Dawson parentage but contextually corroborates it: the same couple (John Dawson + Jane Corlett) named as Susanna's parents in the 1839 christening register were a married couple seven years before her birth, consistent with paternity. It also supplies the BCG-required parents' marriage record, confirming the couple's union and providing the mother's maiden name (Corlett).

### Analysis and Correlation

Two independent acts — the 1839 christening and the 1860 marriage — name "John Dawson" as Susanna's father. The informants differ: John Dawson himself (1839, presenting parent) and Susanna Dawson (1860, bride). The events are separated by twenty-one years and recorded in different register series for different life events. No competing candidate for Susanna's father appeared in any searched source. The parents' 1832 marriage (a third independent act) establishes the couple existed seven years before Susanna's birth and supplies the mother's maiden name (Corlett), which neither the marriage register nor later records provide.

### Tier and Limitation

One of the two direct-parentage sources (the 1860 marriage, src_002) is classified as derivative in this project — its index was accessed via FamilySearch rather than the original register image, and that image was not independently read. A proved tier requires two or more independent original sources with primary information directly agreeing on the specific fact. The 1839 christening register (original, primary, direct) meets that standard for a single source; a second independent original source directly stating the parentage has not been accessed in its original form. Examining the christening register image (ark:/61903/3:1:9396-CBL3-F) and the marriage register image (ark:/61903/3:1:S3HY-65T3-MR8) to confirm both indexed entries against the handwritten originals would advance the conclusion to proved.

---
^[1] "Isle of Man, Parish Registers, 1598-2009", FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XZ5P-PRJ : accessed 2026-07-28), Entry for Susanna Dawson and John Dawson, 10 Mar 1839.

^[2] "Isle of Man, Parish Registers, 1598-2009," FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XZTM-G54 : accessed 28 July 2026), entry for John Kneale and Susanna Dawson, marriage 21 Oct 1860, Lezayre, Isle of Man; citing Isle of Man Civil Registry, Douglas; FamilySearch CID 1784428.

^[3] "Isle of Man, Parish Registers, 1598-2009," FamilySearch (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XZ15-BXY : accessed 28 July 2026), John Dawson and Jane Corlett marriage, 16 August 1832, Ballaugh, Isle of Man; citing Ballaugh Parish Register, image, FamilySearch.

quirks: Civil registration of births and deaths began 1878; marriages not until 1884. All pre-1878 marriage research relies solely on Church of England parish registers.
Marriage license paperwork did not survive for the Isle of Man. Banns are the standard pre-1878 procedure; look for both the banns register and the marriage register.
Couples typically married in the bride's parish. Search Lezayre parish first for Susanna Dawson, who was born there.

From the mid-1800s, Church of England marriage register entries include the names and occupations of the fathers of both bride and groom — a single entry may answer both the marriage question and the paternity question simultaneously.

The 'Isle of Man, Marriages, 1606-1911' (CID 1711668) is a legacy collection — index only, no new records or corrections added since 2010. Always verify finds against 'Isle of Man, Parish Registers, 1598-2009' (CID 1784428), which has both index and images.
Isle of Man censuses 1841-1881 are indexed at Ancestry ($) only; FamilySearch 1871 and 1881 England and Wales censuses also cover Isle of Man residents.
Volume_search returned 3,848 volumes for IoM 1840-1880; most are 0% name-indexed and not full-text searchable — browse-only fallback if indexed collections yield no result.
Isle of Man FHS (iomfhs.im) provides free indexes for births (1576-1960), marriages (1576-1960), and wills (1576-1960); check ManxBMD.com as a free supplementary index.
localities.guide_markdown:
## Isle of Man — Locality Guide (1840–1880)

**Jurisdiction:** British Crown dependency; 17 parishes; records kept at parish level. Key parishes for this project: Lezayre (Susanna Dawson born c.1840), Andreas (John Kneale born c.1839), Maughold (includes Ramsey, where family lived 1861–1877).

### Civil Registration Timeline
- Births/deaths: civil registration began **1878**
- Marriages: civil registration began **1884**
- Pre-1878/1884: Church of England parish registers are the sole official source

### FamilySearch Collections
| Collection | CID | Access | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Isle of Man, Parish Registers, 1598-2009 | 1784428 | Index + images | Preferred: current, maintained |
| Isle of Man, Marriages, 1606–1911 | 1711668 | Index only | Legacy; verify vs. 1784428 |
| Isle of Man, Births and Baptisms, 1607-1910 | 1708663 | Index only | Legacy |
| Isle of Man, Deaths and Burials, 1844-1918 | 1708590 | Index only | |

### Marriage Records
- Couples married in bride's parish; search Lezayre first
- No marriage license paperwork survived; banns were the norm
- From mid-1800s: register entries include fathers' names and occupations of both parties — key for paternity research
- External: FindMyPast IoM Marriages 1598-1979 ($); Ancestry Marriage Index 1606-1984 ($); IoMFHS index 1576-1960 (free)

### Baptism Records
- Church of England baptism registers name child, father (with occupation/residence from mid-1800s), and mother's given name (not maiden name)
- FamilySearch CID 1708663 (legacy index) and CID 1784428 (index + images)

### Census
- IoM-specific censuses 1841-1921 indexed at Ancestry ($) only
- FamilySearch 1871/1881 England & Wales censuses cover IoM residents

### Probate / Wills
- IoMFHS wills index 1576-1960 (free); Ancestry wills index 1600-1864 ($)
- FamilySearch Catalog has microfilm images (browse-only)

### Newspapers
- Isle of Man Newspapers 1792-1960 at imuseum.im ($) — useful for marriage notices

### Other
- ManxBMD.com: free online index for births, marriages, deaths
- Volume_search: 3,848 volumes for IoM 1840-1880, most 0% indexed (browse-only fallback)
